changes.reason: Put back the threshold attempts 0–3 ran with. At 0.01 the weakly projecting states are dropped and fewer than 9 remain at some k-point (dis_windows_proj error).

Move the frozen edge from +2.01 eV (inside the d bands, where the truncated model's error peaks) to just above the d-band top (3.87 eV). frozen_capacity shows this fits easily: at most 6 frozen states against 9 functions, even up to 8.5 eV.

diagnosis: Attempt 4 never ran. Raising dis_proj_min from 0.00125 to 0.01 dropped every state whose projectability on the kept orbitals (V 4s, 3d, 4p) was below 0.01. At some k-point that left fewer than 9 states for 9 Wannier functions, so Wannier90 stopped in dis_windows_proj. The 4p orbitals carry very little weight on the parent states (about 0.6 % of the window's composition), so a cut at 0.01 removes too many states. The fix is to put dis_proj_min back to 0.00125, the value attempts 0–3 ran with. Running attempt 3's deck again would only repeat its truncated_hopping_eta2 failure (49.3 meV truncated against 3.9 meV untruncated). In attempts 0, 2 and 3 the dis_proj_max steps (0.95, 0.9, 0.99) all failed that check, so that knob is used up. In attempt 3 the truncated model's error sits in the d manifold: band 7 at k = (0.5, 0, −0.5), about 1.5 eV, is off by up to 330 meV. The frozen edge at +2.01 eV cuts through the middle of the d bands (7–9 run up to 3.5–3.9 eV), and a frozen edge in the middle of a band is a typical source of kinks that need long-range hoppings. So I am also raising dis_froz_max to 4.0 eV, just above the top of the d bands. frozen_capacity shows that even 8.5 eV freezes at most 6 states against 9 functions, so 4.0 eV fits.
